sources.entry: AnythingLLM - All-in-one desktop & Docker AI application with built-in RAG, AI agents, No-code agent builder, MCP compatibility, and more. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker
AnythingLLM | All-in-one AI app to chat with your documents using any LLM, with agents and RAG

summary.one_liner: AnythingLLM is an open-source, all-in-one AI application for chatting with your documents using local or cloud LLMs, with built-in agents, RAG, and multi-user support, available as a desktop app or self-hosted via Docker.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a chat UI for ingesting documents (PDF, TXT, DOCX, etc.) into a vector database and querying them with a choice of LLM providers, including local models run through a built-in engine and many cloud APIs. It includes AI agents, a no-code agent builder, custom agents, and MCP compatibility, plus scheduled tasks and dynamic model routing. The Docker version adds multi-user support with permissioning, custom themes, and an embeddable chat widget. It offers a developer API and supports multiple embedder, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and vector database options. The monorepo contains a React frontend, a Node/Express server, and a Node document collector service.
use_cases: chat with my private documents using an LLM
run a local ChatGPT-style assistant on my own machine
self-host a multi-user AI chat for a team
build no-code AI agents for workflows
retrieval-augmented generation over PDF and Word files
embed an AI chat widget on my website
notable: Desktop app for Mac, Windows, and Linux, plus Docker self-hosted version
Built-in local LLM engine using Lemonade and llama.cpp with CUDA, Vulkan support
Wide provider support including OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LM Studio, and many others
Multi-user instance with permissioning (Docker version only)
Telemetry can be disabled via DISABLE_TELEMETRY
caveats: Multi-user, custom themes, and embeddable widget are Docker version only
Development setup requires filling in .env files before running
Telemetry is on by default (PostHog) unless disabled; some outbound connections remain even when disabled
